
5f-Block Triple-Zeta Basis Set Archive
======================================


Date: 2 Mar 2007


When publishing work that uses these basis sets, please use the following citation:

K.G. Dyall, Theor. Chem. Acc. (2007) 117:491.
Available from the Dirac web site, http://dirac.chem.sdu.dk.



This archive contains the exponents and the SCF spinor or orbital coefficients, 
given with respect to normalized (spherical or 2-spinor) Gaussian functions, for
the basis sets described in the above article. The SCF functions include the
7p and 6d spinors for all elements. The contractions are taken from SCF 
calculations on a weighted average of the valence configurations:

* For Ac, Pa, U, Np, Cm, and Lr, where the 6d is occupied in the ground state, 
the 5f^n-1 6d^1 7s^2, and 5f^n-1 7p^1 7s^2 configurations were used with a 100:6 
weight ratio. Note that for Ac the 5f is empty: this element is treated as a 
transition metal.

* For Th, the 6d^2 7s^2, 5f^1 6d^1 7s^2 and  6d^1 7s^2 7p^1 configurations were used,
with a weight ratio of 100:10:6

* For the rest (Pu, Am, Cf - No), the 5f^n 7s^2,5f^n-1 6d^1 7s^2, and 
5f^n-1 7p^1 7s^2 configurations were used with a weight ratio of 100:10:6


The archive is set out as follows.

1. Exponents and SCF coefficients for Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave functions, in order
   of Z. The large component functions are given first, followed by the small 
   component functions. Both components are labelled with the large component
   symmetry type, but the primitive functions for the small component are
   those obtained by restricted kinetic balance from the large component.
   The spin-orbit components have a "-" label for j=l-1/2 and a "+" label for
   j=l+1/2.

2. Exponents and SCF coefficients for spin-free modified Dirac-Hartree-Fock wave
   functions, in order of Z. The large component functions are given first, 
   followed by the pseudo-large component functions, then the Foldy-Wouthuysen
   transformed large component functions. Note that all components have the same
   symmetry type. 

3. Exponents of correlating functions for the 5f shell, the 6d and 7s shells, 
   and the 5d shell.

4. Exponents of polarizing functions for the 5f shell and for the 6d and 7s shells.



Basis set construction.
----------------------

Contracted basis sets can be constructed by adding primitive functions to the SCF 
set. These basis sets are described below. Note that the term "quadruple zeta" applies 
to the s and p set; the d set is quintuple zeta and the f set sextuple zeta. This is 
a result of keeping a reasonable energy balance for the basis sets. 

NOTE: Functions are counted from the function with the smallest exponent to the largest. 


1. Valence. The valence space is split into two spatial regions, the outer containing
   the 6d, 7s, and 7p, and the inner containing the 5f, 6s, and 6p. The uncontracted
   functions for these two sets are described separately. However, because all these 
   shells are active or semi-active, the description below should be regarded as a 
   single contracted set. 5f flexibility is not included for Ac, which is a transition
   metal, but it is included for Th because the 5f is low-lying. 

   To the SCF occupied set, add the following:

   For 6d/7s correlation
   1st and 3rd s primitives from the SCF set 
   2nd and 3rd p primitives from the SCF set
   1st and 2nd d primitives from the SCF set
   1st and 2nd f primitives from the SCF set (correlating 2f for Ac)
   Correlating g function for the 6d and 7s shells.

   For 6s/6p/5f correlation
   4th and 6th s primitives from the SCF set 
   5th and 6th p primitives from the SCF set
   3rd and 4th d primitives from the SCF set
   3rd, 4th, and 5th f primitives from the SCF set (3rd only for Ac)
   Correlating 2g1h functions for the 5f shell (except for Ac).

   The combined set for all except Ac is therefore:
   1st, 3rd, 4th and 6th s primitives from the SCF set 
   2nd, 3rd, 5th and 6th p primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th d primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th f primitives from the SCF set
   Correlating g function for the 6d and 7s shells.
   Correlating 2g1h functions for the 5f shell.

   The combined set for Ac is:
   1st, 3rd, 4th and 6th s primitives from the SCF set 
   2nd, 3rd, 5th and 6th p primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th d primitives from the SCF set
   1st, 2nd, and 3rd f primitives from the SCF set
   Correlating g function for the 6d and 7s shells.


   This set is likely to display linear dependence in the d and f sets.
   If this is the case, and your software does not automatically delete
   linearly dependent basis functions, delete either the 6d contraction, 
   or do not uncontract one of the first four primitives; and do not 
   uncontract the 3rd f primitive. 

   There is also likely to be linear dependence in the g set for Pa - Pu.
   If this is the case, delete the innermost g from the 6d/7s correlating set.

2. Valence + 5d correlation.  This set adds functions for correlating the 5d. 
   Excitations from the 5d into the 5f shell are important for correlating the 5f. 

   To basis set 1, add the following:
   7th and 9th s primitives from the SCF set 
   8th and 9th p primitives from the SCF set
   6th and 7th d primitives from the SCF set
   4th and 5th f primitives from the SCF set (Ac only - already in other sets)

   The core correlating g function is close enough to the inner g from the 5f 
   correlating set that extra functions are not needed. For Ac, a g function
   with exponent 2.8130106E+00 should be added. 

3. Dipole polarization of the 5f. Add the polarizing h function. 

   The polarizing h function plays a role in the actinyls at the SCF level, because
   it is the lowest polarizing function for the ungerade (5f/6p-containing) orbitals. 
   The polarizing g function for the 5f is mostly covered by the correlating g 
   function for the 6d. If required, add it for the late actinides.

4. Dipole polarization of the 6d. Add the polarizing f and g functions.






Dirac-Hartree-Fock basis sets           
=============================
